subject: Post-close AR staging gap & journal split plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-close AR staging gap & journal split plan

Team —

During the post-bill run sweep I noticed an unexpected unapplied balance showing in AR staging for the NimbusCloud account: ~€1,182,540 (EUR). It looks like two credit memos and one partial refund from the August run landed in staging and were not reallocated to invoices; downstream RevRec mapping flagged the revenue as recognized against the wrong entity.

Key facts:
- System extract attached (AR_gap_matrix.csv) with row-level IDs.
- Two credits: CM-99821 (partner discount) and CM-100112 (pricing correction).
- One refund R-7745 for a cancelled seat.
- The RevRec mapping rules currently apply by invoice entity_id; because the staging entries lack invoice links they were pushed to the top-level revenue bucket, inflating EU recognized revenue for the wrong legal entity.

Proposed temporary approach before month close:
1) Create a pair of reversing/allocating journal entries that move the staging credits into the correct entity-level AR accounts (one JV to split the credits across entities A/B). Mark these as "post-close true-up" and hold in a suspense clearing account until GL owner sign-off.
2) Update RevRec input mapping by adding a deterministic fallback that picks the customer_entity from payment trace if invoice_id is null (short-term rule).
3) Engage Payments (ClearWave) to confirm whether the refund has an original invoice pointer they can surface.

Requesting:
- Marcus: can you own the JV draft and confirm tax treatment for the credit split?
- Grace: can you review VAT implications for the refund reallocation in EU (reverse charge / reclaim?)
- Laura: please confirm if this needs to be a FY-end disclosure item or a routine month-close adjustment.

Timeline: we should have a sign-off and temporary entries posted by EOD 21 Sep. If we can't get the right support data from ClearWave, we'll do the suspense route and follow with a corrective posting next close.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: AR_gap_matrix.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close AR staging gap & journal split plan

Thanks Vanessa —

I pulled the rows and ran a quick trace against the payment ledger. A few quick notes:
- I see the two credit memos were issued by Sales Ops under the old customer_entity mapping (pre-entity-split). That explains why invoice_id is null on the staging rows.
- Refund R-7745 has an original payment_id (pm_44321) but the link to invoice iv_22018 was lost during the migration from the legacy billing table.

Plan from my side:
- I'll draft the journal entries and include a pair of contra-lines: one to clear the unapplied staging (suspense AR code 2100-999) and one to allocate the amounts to entity A (4100-A) and entity B (4100-B) proportionally per the attached AR_gap_matrix.
- Tax treatment: for the credits I'll propose to treat them as credit memo adjustments (reduce AR and reduce recognized revenue) — will defer to Grace on VAT specifics for the refund.

I'll attach a first-pass workbook (journal_entries_draft.xlsx) by EOD today and flag lines that should be manual postings. If legal or tax want a separate disclosure we'll follow their lead.

On ClearWave: Vanessa, can you loop them in with the payment_id list so they can confirm whether the invoice pointers exist on their side? If they do, we may not need a suspense hold.

—Marcus

Attachment: journal_entries_draft.xlsx (Excel, 85KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close AR staging gap & journal split plan

Appreciate the heads-up. A few VAT/tax points from EU perspective:
- Refund R-7745: if the original sale was zero-rated (export) then reclaim mechanics are different vs. standard-rated — need to validate the original invoice tax code. If ClearWave can give us invoice_id, that will settle treatment.
- Credit memos that correct pricing should reduce taxable base in the period they are applied; if we post a post-close JV we need to ensure the VAT rate applies to the period of the sale (not the JV posting date). That may require a historical VAT adjustment in the tax module.

Suggested mechanics:
1) Post the JV to move the amounts into the correct entity's AR ledger, but include a VAT rate flag on the JV lines so tax can pick up and post a historical adjustment (separate tax journal).
2) For the refund, if ClearWave returns the invoice pointer we'll do an invoice-level apply rather than a JV. If not, we'll treat the refund as a cash refund and post a reclaim where applicable.

I can coordinate with TaxOps but will need the attachment Marcus creates with the GL accounts and the mapping table. Happy to be the approver for the VAT treatment.

- Grace
Head of Tax & Treasury
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: acct-recon@acmecloud.com, payments@clearwave.com
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close AR staging gap & journal split plan — decision and owners

Update and decisions (final before we post):

1) ClearWave confirmed refund R-7745 has original invoice pointer iv_22018 and that pointer is tied to the pre-migration entity. They provided a CSV mapping (pointers_7745.csv) via their portal. Good news — we can apply the refund at invoice level.

2) For the two credit memos (CM-99821, CM-100112) we do not have invoice pointers. Per discussion above:
   - Marcus will post a pair of JVs that move the credits from staging (2100-999) to entity-level AR accounts (4100-A, 4100-B) and include a VAT rate flag on each JV line.
   - Grace will coordinate the historical VAT adjustment entry after the JV is posted. TaxOps will create a separate tax journal referencing the JV batch id.

3) Laura confirmed this is a routine month-close adjustment (not a material FY disclosure) given the amount and root cause (legacy mapping).

Action items & owners:
- Marcus: post JVs by COB 25 Sep and mark batch as "post-close true-up: NimbusCloud". (owner)
- Grace: prepare VAT historical adjustment journal and sign-off on tax treatment by 28 Sep. (owner)
- Vanessa: follow up with Accounting to reconcile AR ledger after JVs and close the Jira ticket SUP-1234. (owner)

Links:
- Drive folder with workbooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_drive_link
- Jira: SUP-1234 (post-close AR gap)

I'll post the final JV batch id into this thread once complete and notify Legal if they want to review the customer communications.

Thanks everyone — good coordination.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
